_about: The yearly Pinterest calendar (owner request 2026-09-24): seasons with release windows timed ahead of Pinterest searches (Trends, US, weekly, pulled 2026-09-24), the daily board mix, the review-tag vocabulary and the content bank. scripts/pins-plan.mjs turns it into each day's instructions; docs/pinterest-runbook.md explains the loop. Items: ref = the passage (verse art uses its start verse), moment = what to draw (scenes) or the decorations (verse art), variants = codes from `variants` in the order to make them, priority 1-3, seasons = season ids or 'evergreen' (an item with no evergreen only goes out inside its seasons). The daily task may add items (refill) but never removes used ones.
_trends: Search peaks (Pinterest Trends US, Sept 2025 - Sept 2026): Christmas coloring rises Nov 10, peak Dec 15; Epiphany Dec 29 - Jan 12; New Year verse Jan 5; Valentine crafts Jan 19 - Feb 16 (peak Feb 9); Sunday school lessons peak Feb 23 (Lent planning); Mother's Day crafts May 4-11; Pentecost May 25; VBS crafts Apr 27 - Jul 13 (peak Jun 8); David and Goliath craft peak Jun 22; Father's Day crafts Jun 15-22; back to school peak Aug 3; Noah's ark and Jonah crafts peak Sep - Oct; Halloween crafts Oct 27; Thanksgiving crafts Nov 3 - Dec 1 (peak Nov 24); Bible verse coloring pages year-round, highest in Sept. Our own data: Genesis 1-4 Pins earn 62% of clicks, peaking in September. Windows open ~6 weeks before the rise because a new Pin needs weeks to be distributed.
_tags: The visual profile given to every approved page at review (pins.json `tags`, or pin-learn.json `profiles` for older Pins), so the learning loop can find what makes a page work: characters = named people drawn; children = a child among them; animals = any animal; scale = how much of the page the main figures fill (large > 40%, small < 15%); viewpoint = close (faces and hands), medium (full figures and near setting), wide (figures small in a big scene); setting = how much of the page the story's place fills; density = amount to color; faces = the main expression; feel = the page's mood at a glance; composition = the main layout; action = someone is doing something vs posing; recognizable = the story is obvious at feed size without the title; look = the drawing's style family; lines = visual line weight; frame = the border; caption = a reference caption on the page; layout, motifs = verse art only.
